Name: Office CMBS DQ
Notes: NEW RECORD. Exceeds prior ATH of 11.76% (Oct 2025). +211 bps YoY. Office the largest contributor to net delinquencies ($1.6B net increase in Jan). Relentless deterioration continues.

Name: Bank CRE 90+ DQ
Notes: RQ-001 RESOLVED. 1.56% (DRCRELEXFACBS) = all banks, all CRE incl owner-occupied. 4.18% (FDIC QBP) = large banks >$250B, non-owner-occupied only = correct CMBS comparator. Masking gap = 7.1pp (vs CMBS office 11.31%). Declining from 4.99% peak (Q3 2024), 4th consecutive decline. Pre-pandemic: 0.59%. Small banks: 1.14% DQ but 1,788 exceed 300% CRE/equity. Mods suppress bank DQ (66% increase through Q2 2025; $39.3B modified balance, +86% YoY).

Name: Multifamily CMBS DQ
Notes: Rising again after brief Oct peak (7.12%). +232bps YoY = stress spreading beyond office. Sunbelt oversupply: Austin 15.3% vacancy (worst nationally), Atlanta 12%, Phoenix/Nashville ~10-12%. Pipeline collapsing (starts -40%+) = supply relief coming. $115B loans with DSCR <1.20x maturing by end 2026. Two-thirds of MF foreclosures = 2021-22 vintage. RQ-012: MF insurance +119% since pre-pandemic.

Name: Office Vacancy Rate
Notes: RQ-006/011 enriched. BIFURCATION EXTREME: Trophy 12-14% & tightening. Class B 20-25% & flat/worsening. Class C 25-35% & worsening. SF: trophy 15.3% vs overall 35.1% (20pp gap). Manhattan: trophy 55% of leasing (up from 38%). Chicago: trophy rents +26% since 2020 vs market +1%. Trophy = 2-4% of stock. Class B = 40-45%, C = 15-20%. B/C breakeven at ~75-80% occupancy — many at/below. Bottom-tier B/C obsolescence is PERMANENT. CMBS office DQ 11.76% (exceeds GFC peak by 106bps). AI DEMAND: 7M SF in SF (12% of stock), 35% of SF leasing, 80% of newly leased. AI durable 2-3yr but 20-30% contraction risk 2027-28. Structural floor from big tech AI divisions (30-40%). AI is gateway-city positive only — does NOT solve B/C or secondary markets.

Name: CRE Modification Volume
Notes: RQ-007/008 enriched. UPGRADE TO RED. Bank mods +66% YoY ($16.7B→$27.7B). Securitized +86% YoY. Q3 volume $11.2B. 67% are extensions. Small banks +217% mod rate (vs large +14%). Mods grew 326.9% in 2024. Full payoffs -53.1%. $64.6B in CMBS special servicing (surpassed GFC peak). ASU 2022-02 disclosure cliff Dec 2025 = visibility will DROP as maturity wall peaks. Q4 10-Ks PENDING.

Name: Modification Re-Default Rate
Notes: RQ-008 enriched. ~One-third of recent mods re-default. $5.5B re-defaults = decade high. Avg payment relief on re-defaulted mods only ~2% (insufficient). FDIC historical: >30% of modified RE loans subsequently foreclosed. Loss severity on re-defaults: 49.7-63% (far exceeds GFC ~33%). CRED iQ: "early part of the curve." Extensions (67% of mods) don't fix valuation problems. Institutional defaults ($15-20B+) confirm — even Brookfield/PIMCO walk away rather than inject equity.

Name: CRE Maturity Wall
Notes: RQ-002/003 RESOLVED. $936B breakdown: MF ~32% ($300B), Office ~14-20% ($130-187B), Banks ~48% ($452B). 40-50% is 2021-22 vintage. H1 ~$375B / H2 ~$560B. Refi gap: base case $336B (36%); realistic capacity $500-700B. Forced recognition $140-250B over 2026-27. 30-40% fail DSCR at 1.25x (148bps rate gap = 16.3% DS increase). 20-30% of wall is extended loans. 1,788 banks >300% CRE/equity. Each 50bps Fed cut = $50-75B additional capacity. Office 20-30% foreclosure rate. NOT 2008 but largest forced recognition since GFC.

Name: CMBS Maturity Default Rate
Current: Office: only 44% paid on time; 51% outstanding past maturity. SB default rate 12.9% (office 19.7%)
Notes: RQ-007/009 enriched. UPGRADE TO RED. Only 44% of 2025 office maturities paid on time (vs 72% all property). 51% still outstanding past maturity. KBRA SB default rate: 12.9% (doubled from 6.4%); office 19.7% (up from 1.9% = 10x). JPM estimate: ~$39B CMBS office (21%) will default. Loss severity 49.7-63% (far exceeds GFC). Institutional strategic defaults accelerating ($15-20B+). Peak expected H1 2026.

Name: Office Lease Expiration Schedule
Notes: UPGRADE FROM YELLOW. Scale much larger than initial estimate. Manhattan alone: 46.4M sf 2025-2027. Tenants took short-term renewals 2022-24 pushing expirations forward. 85.5M sf expiring 2025.

Name: Open-End Fund Hidden Losses
Current: $130-217B (improving: BREIT gates lifted, ODCE positive returns)
Notes: RQ-010 enriched. BREIT meeting all redemptions since early 2024 = positive. ODCE had 3 consecutive quarters positive total return. But: SREIT NAV -40% from peak ($8.8B), $999M redemption queue (11.6% NAV), only 3-4% fulfilled, redemption limits cut to 0.33%/month. Moody's downgraded Blackstone (Ba2→Ba3), Apollo, KKR CRE funds — rising problem loans. CRE debt outperforming equity: 2022 vintage 11.3% median IRR (debt) vs 2.1% (equity). Non-traded REIT sector: $2.8B redemption requests vs $1.2B inflows (Q1 2025). FSB (Jun 2025): non-bank CRE investors "could amplify financial risks in a downturn."

Name: Fund Redemption Queue
Current: Declining (BREIT gates lifted; ODCE queues shrinking via rescissions)
Notes: IMPROVING: BREIT gates fully lifted. ODCE queues declining as returns turned positive. High rescission rates = investors choosing to stay. Peaked at 19.3% (worse than GFC's 15%).

Name: CRE CLO Issuance
Notes: RQ-010 enriched. Market reopened dramatically. Jan 2025 alone $5.4B (more than half of 2024 total $8.7B). Total CMBS+CLO issuance $125.6B in 2025 (+21% YoY). BUT underlying quality diverging: CRE CLO non-performing matured loans at 43% of matured balances (+720bps surge). 66.3% of allocated CRE CLO loan balances ($3.8B) in matured loans. 76% of floating-rate CRE CLO is MF. SMBC provides ~90% of rate cap agreements (concentration risk). 40% of rate caps expire before loan maturity (~700 loans/$30B+). Record Q2 2025 issuance ($8.9B) = new vintage confidence despite legacy distress. Bifurcation: legacy CLOs distressed, new issuance healthy.

Name: HOA/Condo Special Assessments
Notes: RQ-005 enriched. Crisis is self-reinforcing cycle. 1,438 FL buildings on Fannie blacklist (doubled in 2yr; ~700 in South FL). FL #1 nationally in foreclosures — 8 consecutive months rising (+57% YoY). Condo prices -9.9% YoY (worst since 2009). 7 of 10 worst US metros are FL. Cape Coral -31% from peak (below 2006 bubble). Insurance +164% (Miami-Dade). ~28K associations, ~1.5M units. FHA DQ >11%. Super-lien subordinates mortgages. Buildings <30yr +10% value; >30yr severe declines. Bank exposure UNQUANTIFIED.

Name: Office-to-Resi Conversion
Notes: UPGRADE FROM GREEN. NYC: 4.1M sf through Aug 2025 (2.5x 2024). Policy support expanding (NYC 90% tax exemptions, DC 20yr abatements). 10-15% of office buildings suitable. Becoming a material supply-side factor for vacancy relief.
